changes: A Study session stops at the end of each topic. A card lets you keep going or stop there, and Today picks up where you stopped.
Questions from topics you learned earlier come back when they're due, up to 3 a day. godspeed asks and checks them itself.
When the teacher quotes your lecture, that page shows in the lesson with the quoted words highlighted.
The teacher can show a plot. You guess first, then the plot opens.
After a right answer the teacher can leave you one sentence to keep, sometimes with a short phrase to remember it by. You can drop an analogy or a phrase you don't like.
Open Claude Code opens a helper beside the teacher that reads files and builds the graph, so the teacher keeps teaching. Web search can use your own Tavily key, in Settings, Connection.
godspeed now runs on Intel Macs, with its own download.
Buttons look like keys that sink when clicked, the space head shows its signature on every tab, and the Lessons tab is tidier.
A second lesson no longer waits minutes for its first reply while your agent is still on the first one.
godspeed is a new app underneath. It looks and works the same, and the download is about a quarter of the size.
Your spaces, lessons and settings carry over. The first time the new app opens, it saves a copy of your data before it changes anything.
On a Mac it arrives like any update and needs macOS 14 or newer.
On Windows and Linux, download it once and install it. It takes the place of the old app, and after that it updates by itself.
godspeed has a new look. A top bar replaces the sidebar, with Today, a tab for each space, Follow, the teacher and Menu, and Settings, Appearance has a Paper and a Night background.
Classes are now called spaces, since you can study anything in one, like a course, a certification or a language. Your classes move over by themselves.
Today is one list of what's due next across every space, each with one button to start and a Done stamp you can undo. Deadlines further out sit under Later.
Each space has tabs for Progress, Lessons, Files, Graph, Cheat sheets and Deadlines. On Deadlines you add, change, mark done and delete them.
A lesson is the reading on the left and the teacher on the right, with one writing box for every message, answer and piece of work.

Prepare for something, in the menu, makes a prep for one interview or test. The teacher looks it up and writes a prep sheet with the topics to study, and you take timed mocks like the real thing. Code questions run their examples on your computer, and Go over it studies what you got wrong.
When the teacher uses your space's files or a web page, a small number marks it. Click it to see that page. The sources are listed under the message.

In study, each topic starts the way that fits it, whether it's a term, a method, an idea or a proof. A problem you gave up on comes back in a new form, and the session ends by asking where you'd use one of today's topics.
A wrong guess on a prediction question no longer counts as a mistake.
A space shows when the teacher is reading its files and what it made, on the space, on Today and in Talk.
If you start your agent through a launcher, Change command under the Open Claude Code button sets the command godspeed runs.
The new logo is a pixel g on a paper tile. The teacher has no mascot anymore, only its name and what it's doing.

The next godspeed is a new app. A Mac on macOS 14 or newer moves to it like any update, and an older Mac keeps this version. On Windows and Linux, godspeed tells you when the new app is ready to download, and your spaces and lessons stay.
Every problem now shows by itself on the right, in Study and Practice too, like homework. You work on it in the one message box at the bottom.

A message you send while a problem is open is your work on it, not a side question. The teacher can check it, close the problem or switch to the part you asked for, and you never have to discard a problem first.

The teacher answers the exact thing you asked first, follows your own method when it works, and keeps replies short when you're stuck. After one explanation that didn't land, it asks one small question to find what's confusing you.
Problem sets start at the first problem and its first part unless you pick another.
The teacher looks up how your class teaches something before explaining it, and uses your class's own words and method.
When an explanation isn't landing, the teacher stops explaining and asks one small question to find exactly what's confusing you.
Homework: when the assignment file isn't attached yet, the teacher finds it in your class files and attaches it.
Lessons use much less of your agent's memory. The class card no longer lists every file, and saving a rule or shortening a lesson no longer sends the whole lesson again.
Long lessons no longer make you wait. godspeed shortens the older part at once, and the teacher's written summary takes its place a few minutes later.
Open Claude Code also opens a backup teacher. When the main one stops to compact its memory, the backup answers your lesson and Talk messages so you don't wait.
Buttons are a step brighter, so they stand out from the text around them.
The attach and send buttons in the lesson's message box sit evenly inside it.

Homework: the whole problem stays in the Your turn panel while you work, so you never scroll up to find it. You work in the message box under the lesson, and the teacher checks each message and marks the problem done when your work is right.
The panel shows which part of a problem you're on, like q3 (b), and scrolls to it.
Math like 0<r<n no longer cuts off the rest of the teacher's message.
The teacher in the sidebar says what it's doing in a speech bubble, with talk and follow side by side.
Buttons that looked like plain text, like discard problem, skip question, cancel and try again, now look like buttons.
A calculator in every box you write in. End a calculation with = and the answer shows in grey after it. Click it or press Tab to keep it, or keep typing to skip it.

It works out numbers, letters you set on a line above (x = 3), expanding and simplifying, solve 2x + 3 = 11, derivatives (d/dx x^3 =) and integrals (int x^2 dx =). Exact answers come with their decimal.
A long problem shows in full in the lesson, where code and every part fit. The Your turn panel shows how it starts with a show the whole problem button, so the box you work in keeps its room.
Text that scrolls in the Your turn panel fades out before it reaches the panel's border and title.
Buttons are solid rounded blocks instead of text in brackets.
The sidebar is easier to scan: class names are bold, a class's pages hang off one line under it, and add class and settings sit quieter in their own group at the bottom.
On a Mac the window buttons sit in the middle of the top bar.
The bar under a question no longer covers the panel's border.

One message box in lessons: it sits under the lesson and never moves. If a question or problem is open, what you send is a side question and the question stays open. Talk is hidden while a lesson is open.
You can ask the teacher to add, move or remove a deadline in the middle of a lesson.

Homework mode: pick a homework or project's assignment file on its page and hit work on. The teacher lists its problems and opens them one at a time. You do the work, typed or as a photo, and the teacher checks it with hints but never gives you the answer. A problem counts as done once your own work is right.
Homework and projects show how many problems are done, on Home, on their page and beside the lesson. Mark done when you've handed it in.

The Graph page lays topics out in columns by level, from what you learn first to what builds on it. Pick a topic to see what it needs and what it leads to, or open a fact to see where it came from, its answers and a button to practice it.
The class Overview is tighter, so it fits on one screen.

A new look: godspeed now looks like a terminal app, with monospace type, panes with their names cut into the border and [ bracket ] buttons. The first time you open this version, a short boot screen plays and then the new look draws in.
The top bar shows where you are as a path you can click, and the left column holds your classes as a tree, your lessons with a + study button, and the teacher with follow and talk.
The teacher mascot is now a pixel character.

Home shows what's due next with a big countdown, everything else coming up with how ready you are, a grid of every fact in each class colored by how often you get it right, and what you and your agent did lately.
In a lesson the steps sit beside the text, how sure you are is five numbered buttons, and side questions open at the bottom of the right column.
The activity list is saved, so it's still there after a restart.
godspeed is dark only now. If you used Paper or White, it switches to Black.
Browser tab titles read like the top bar, like godspeed / graph.
If a class's linked folder gets no new files for 4 days, a pop-up tells you, with buttons to open the folder or see the class's files. Closing it hides it for another 4 days.
When files disappear from a class's linked folder, a pop-up says which ones.
The Files page has a Recent changes list with every file added or removed in the last 14 days.
Ask your agent in Talk to work on something, like a problem set, and it starts the lesson in the right class and opens it for you.
When godspeed asks your agent by itself what a deadline covers, it now waits until Talk has been quiet for 10 minutes, so it never cuts into your conversation.
Opening a lesson from another class switches the sidebar to that class, so the lesson shows up in the list.
With deadlines from more than one class, Due soon in the sidebar shows each deadline's name first and its class after it, so names like Quiz 4 no longer get cut off.
A calmer lesson screen. Send now sits inside each writing box instead of a big bar under it, the top bar has no more white blocks, and lessons and deadlines in the sidebar fit on one line.
The cheat sheet beside a lesson has one clear title, fits its pages to the panel and keeps its zoom buttons under them.
With the cheat sheet open, the lesson text no longer gets squeezed away. When the window is too narrow, the problem moves below the text.
Cleaner screens. The small bold labels like Your turn and Thinking while reading are gone, and the section names that stay are plain text at normal size.

Each cheat sheet has its own chat. Ask your agent what something on the sheet means, or tell it what to change, and it answers or makes a new version. It looks over every page and checks the formulas against your class before sending.
Point at the sheet. Drag a box over the part that confuses you and it goes with your message as a picture.
Things you say should always hold, like A4 both sides or no slang, are saved as rules for that sheet. You can see them and remove them.
Open your cheat sheet right next to a lesson, study or practice session with the Cheat sheet button. Questions you ask there include the problem you're on.
A newer PDF in the sheet's folder, say from editing it outside godspeed, shows up as a new version.
Each class has a Cheat sheets page in the sidebar. It shows every deadline, coming up first, with a preview of its sheet, or Make one when there isn't a sheet yet.
Show in Finder replaces Save as PDF, since your sheet is already a PDF on your computer.

Cheat sheets are real PDFs now. Your agent makes the file itself (LaTeX works great) in a folder it keeps, so changes edit the same sheet, and godspeed shows that exact PDF. Print and Save as PDF use the same file.
The cheat sheet studio is a canvas you can drag around and zoom, with Zoom to fit. Your last few versions sit next to the new one so you can compare them.

Cheat sheets are made from a prompt now. Say what you want, like both sides of A4 with a flowchart for any problem, and your agent lays it out, reading your syllabus for the rules and putting your weak topics and mistakes first. Ask for changes the same way, and if a page runs over, one click makes it fit.

Cheat sheets take your own instructions, like "put Bayes' rule first" or "use my professor's notation". Write them when you set it up or in the studio, and Remake sheet makes it again with them. Pinned blocks stay.
You can add pictures and PDFs to your answers, to the start page's topic box, and to Talk. Files you add wait for you if you leave and come back.
The lesson box, the side question box and Talk format math as you type.
Picking facts on the start page is enough to start studying, no topic needed.
Talk keeps what you typed, offers Try again when a reply fails, and Stop or Esc actually stops the reply.
Stop shows in the practice box whenever the teacher is working, and study sessions say Continue instead of Next problem.
The cheat sheet says when no agent is connected instead of spinning, and its change box sends on Enter.

You can ask your teacher something while a practice problem is open, with the same box as under lesson questions, pictures and PDFs included. The problem and your thinking stay put, and asking doesn't count as a hint.

Cheat sheets. When an exam lets you bring one, click Cheat sheet on its deadline page. Your agent reads the rules from your syllabus, you check them, and it writes a sheet that puts your past mistakes and weak topics first and leaves out what you already know cold.

The sheet shows at its real size with a note beside each block saying why it's there, and a meter shows if it still fits. Click a block to tighten it, redo it or ask for a change, then print it or save it as a PDF.
You can add pictures and PDFs in Talk and in the box for asking your teacher something while a question is open, the same way as in a lesson. Drag them in or paste them too.

Studying for a deadline picks up where you left off. When your last Study session for it isn't finished, the button says "Continue studying for Midterm · 1 of 4 topics" and opens that session. Once it's done, the button starts the next topics.

New lesson and Practice are now one Study button. Pick a deadline ("Study for Midterm") or type any topic, and your teacher decides for each topic: one you've never been tested on gets a short explanation with a worked example first, then a problem. A weak one goes straight to problems with hints, and a strong one gets one quick check.
Studying for a deadline takes about four topics at a time in the order your class covered them. Click it again and it moves on to the next topics that still need work.
Your old lessons and practice sessions work like before, and the sidebar now shows when a practice problem is waiting for you.
The last answers of a short lesson now always reach your graph, even when the app restarts soon after or a save is already running. A practice problem that names an idea twice counts once for it.
Code, diagrams and Edit class are readable on the Paper and White backgrounds, and math that's too wide scrolls instead of getting cut off.
Sending a message while a question is open closes that question, the same way your teacher sees it. After a side question the Teaching line stays where it was.
A new lesson's topic is sent only once, practice problems have a Stop button while your teacher writes, and the thinking box keeps its size in a short window.
Names that get cut off show in full when you hover them, the sidebar no longer slides in every time the app opens, and a link to a removed lesson or deadline shows a page with Go Home.
File groups aren't named after small words like "and" anymore, Save problems in Edit class scroll into view, and your agent's notes are kept if their file ever breaks.
Practice now counts toward being ready. A problem you solve counts as right for the ideas it uses, and one you give up on or skip counts as wrong.
Problems you solve with hints don't move your percentage either way, but your teacher sees them for two weeks so it can bring them back.

Questions now count toward being ready even when your teacher didn't re-explain the idea first. When a lesson is saved to your graph, your agent also says which ideas each question tested, so warm-up questions and exam practice move your deadline's percentage.
Lessons you already had get their questions read once, the next time your agent connects.

Short lessons now count toward being ready. What a lesson taught gets saved to your graph once it sits for 5 minutes, not only after a long stretch, so the questions you answered show up on your deadlines.
Lessons that were never saved get caught up as soon as your agent connects.
When a deadline has nothing linked, godspeed asks your agent to work out what's on it from your files, by itself. You'll see that request in Talk, from godspeed, not you.
A deadline's page shows what's on it as class days by week, so a day's slides, transcript and discussion are one row, and it names the file your agent went by.
Class days before an exam that aren't on it get flagged, each with Add or Leave out. Once every day is on it or left out, the page says so.
Your agent works out what a deadline covers from your files first, like a practice exam or the syllabus, and only asks you when they don't say.
A deadline with nothing linked no longer lists every file. Ask your teacher to work it out, or pick the files yourself.
No more false "look missing" warnings from numbered file names.
Talk messages reach your agent even while it's working on a lesson. It answers whichever came first, then goes back to the lesson.

The Follow chip shows what your agent is doing right now, like reading a file and how far along it is, and it moves you to the page it just changed. It hides when no agent is connected, and it's the only Follow switch now.
When no agent is connected, the Talk box, New lesson and Your turn each say so, with a button to open it.
Text and colors are easier to read on every theme, switches clearly show on and off, and marks that used color alone now have a shape too.
Better keyboard and screen reader support: dialogs keep and return focus, menus and tabs behave like menus and tabs, notices stay while you look at them, and each page has its own title.
The teacher panel makes room for the page instead of covering it, and the teacher moves out of the way of buttons.
The Graph fits its topics at a readable size, and the Where you're at panel can be hidden.
Edit class opens on the deadline you clicked, and a deadline's file list has a heading and a filter.

Fewer repeated labels: one name for topics you haven't been tested on, each deadline shows once on Home, plain words instead of technical ones in lessons and the fact list, and "Add files" everywhere.
Smaller windows get more room: the sidebar closes below 1000 pixels wide and long lists drop their progress bars first.
Classes can now hold Word and PowerPoint files, code files like .c, .py and .java, and plain text files with no extension. Everything is read on your computer.

While your agent reads a new file from a linked folder, it also sorts out course logistics like announcements, emails and schedules. Those become course info, so they never turn into quiz questions, but your teacher can still read them. A kind you pick yourself always stays.
Your teacher's daily note lists new course info apart from new study files, so it knows about things like a moved exam.
A lecture video whose transcript is already in the class isn't transcribed again. It uses the transcript.
A linked folder names the files it can't read, and tells you Google Docs need saving as PDF or Word first.
If Google Drive is paused or offline, the Files page says it isn't responding, and nothing is removed.
Files in a linked folder's subfolders that aren't part of a numbered series are grouped by their folder, and file names with dates like 20260924 are read as dates.
Textbook chapters no longer get paired with lecture transcripts just because their numbers match.
Your godspeed folder has a classes folder with shortcuts to every class file, grouped like the Files page, so you and your agent can find them. Show in Finder on the Files page opens it.
Link a class to its Google Drive folder and new course files show up on their own. Files you already added aren't added twice and keep what you studied.
A new file joins its series, so a new homework sheet is course info like the others and a new lecture is study material.

The Files page says which folder it's watching and when it last checked, marks new files as New for 3 days, and shows how many came in since you last looked. The sidebar's Files row gets a dot until you open it.
When new files come in you get a notice, a row in Activity, and your teacher hears about them. If no agent is connected they wait and get read when it connects.
If Google Drive is offline or still starting, nothing is deleted. Files still downloading wait until they finish, and renaming a file keeps its facts.

Each deadline has its own page. Click its ring on the Overview or its row in Coming up to see if its lectures, transcripts and discussions are all there, a day by day plan up to it with your weakest topics first, and how ready you are.
Check with the syllabus asks your teacher to compare the syllabus with your files and tell you what's missing.
The Files page groups your files by name, like lectures, discussions and homework. A lecture's notes and transcript share one row with its date, and you can search.
The teacher's panel opens along the right edge as a solid panel, and menus and pop-ups are solid boxes instead of see-through glass.
Once you pick an answer and start writing, your answer and how sure you are fold into one row so the thinking box gets the room. The side question waits behind Ask a side question.
The countdown counts calendar days, so it matches the rest of the app.
Click your teacher to talk to it outside lessons. Ask it to add a class, link a folder of course files, add deadlines from a syllabus, or answer a quick question about your classes.
Every change it makes shows in the chat as a row you can click to go there. Clear starts the chat over.
The teacher can't delete a class or a file from the chat. You still do that yourself.
What your agent is doing now and its recent changes moved to the Activity tab in the same panel.
Your teacher is called Teacher by default. You can still rename it in Settings.
Your thinking turns math into real math as you type. Write 1/2, x^2 or x_1 and it formats when you add a space, and >= becomes ≥.
Type a word like sqrt, choose or pi and a small list pops up. Click one to put it in, and click any math to change it.
Once you pick an answer and start writing, the answer list folds into one row so the thinking box gets more room. Click Change to open it again.
Your saved thinking shows its math properly too.
The lesson meter now shows how big the lesson is next to the point where it gets summarized, which you can change in Settings.
Follow your agent is on by default, and godspeed remembers when you turn it off.
If your lessons or the Teaching instructions can't load, you now see Try again instead of an empty list or greyed out buttons.
A lesson rename that fails keeps the old name and tells you.
Long deadline and class names are cut short with the full name on hover, so menus and Coming up stay tidy.
A diagram still being written shows its loading spinner.
Halley uses less battery while she waits next to a row.
You can now ask your teacher something while a question is waiting. Type in Ask the teacher something under Submit answer, and the question stays open until you answer it.
godspeed opens straight to the welcome screen, which now plays the startup sound. The separate loading screen is gone.
Answered questions show each option's full description, and hidden steps no longer leave empty rows in a reply.
Home, Overview and the activity list stay quicker as your classes grow.
Lots of small fixes in Settings, Edit class and lessons, like buttons that could be clicked twice and fields that stayed editable while saving.
If Node.js isn't installed, Open Claude Code and Open Codex now tell you to install it from nodejs.org instead of waiting forever.
Switching off Web research or PDF reading in Settings now turns them off in practice too, and your teacher stops planning around tools you switched off.
Edit class shows Try again when a class can't load, instead of empty fields.
A blank deadline row no longer blocks Save.
Moving a file with no facts no longer says its facts leave the graph.
Lots of small fixes all over the app, about 150 of them. Most you will never notice, but a few you might.
Stop now works during the very first reply of a lesson, and a lesson no longer gets stuck if a turn fails right after you dismiss a question.
Turning the knowledge graph back on in Settings starts the class files that were waiting, without a restart.
Due soon in the sidebar moves on to the next day after midnight.
Codex stops refusing to start when an old godspeed entry is left in its settings, and the copied start command works for home folders with unusual characters.
Figures, demos and PDF readings fail less often for no good reason, and your teacher handles binary and very large files more carefully.

If the old godspeed plugin is still on your computer, godspeed tells you in the corner and in Settings, with a Remove button. The old plugin let Claude Code chats outside your godspeed folder connect, so the app could say your agent was connected when it wasn't really there.
The same goes for an old godspeed entry in Codex's settings.
Setting up the godspeed folder now removes all of the old plugin, not just part of it.
Classes you made before an update now catch up. The next time your agent connects, it fills in a missing icon, signature or description on its own, and asks you when it isn't sure.
Your teacher can now save a rule on its own when you tell it how you like to learn, like using Python for code examples. It shows in the chat with Undo and Edit.
Claude Code can save rules from the terminal too, and godspeed shows a notice in the corner with Undo and Edit.
Rules your teacher saved are labeled in Settings and in Edit class. Hover the label to see when.
Text now follows your background color. It stays easy to read on any color and takes a hint of that color so it fits in.
Bold and italic colors are made a little lighter or darker if they would be hard to read on your background.
Your agent now has its own folder, ~/godspeed. One click on Open Claude Code makes it and starts Claude Code there in a terminal.
godspeed only loads in that folder, so your other Claude Code and Codex chats stay clean.
A live log under the button shows each step, from making the folder to your agent teaching.
The arrow next to the button switches to Codex, or shows the address and token for any other MCP app.
When no agent is open, the sidebar has an Open in godspeed folder button.
The Claude Code plugin is gone. If you had it, godspeed offers to set up the folder once and removes the plugin for you.
What you type in a lesson is saved as you go, so switching pages or a restart no longer wipes your answer.
Questions have a Skip question button and practice problems have Discard problem, so you never need the Esc key to move on.
If your agent takes a reply and goes quiet for a few minutes, a line next to Stop lets you stop and send again.
When no agent is teaching, the lesson says Waiting for your agent and shows how to connect it, instead of Thinking forever.
The sidebar and Settings show when your agent is connected but not teaching yet.
Unlinking a folder or removing a file asks first and says how many facts go with it.
Edit class asks before throwing away your changes.
Errors say what happened in plain words and come with a Try again button.
Ticking a deadline done shows an Undo for a few seconds.
Lesson rows in the sidebar have a ⋯ button for rename, move, export and delete.
Tab moves between buttons with a visible ring, and dialogs keep Tab inside them.
Plainer words all over, like Warm-up instead of Probe and lesson length in pages instead of tokens.
Long lessons get summarized sooner, so your agent stays fast and cheap.
Agents get smaller work items and Claude Code waits for free, so teaching uses fewer tokens.
godspeed works with the newest MCP version, and Codex and older agents still connect.
If godspeed has to restart after a problem, it tells you instead of replaying the welcome screen, and the crash dialog has Report a bug.
Security updates for Next.js and Electron, and links only open web and email addresses.
Follow no longer gets stuck when your cursor is in a text box. It only waits while you're typing or a dialog is open.
With Follow off, when your agent changes something on another page, the top bar shows what it did with a Go to button.
The white number box next to the class name is gone.
A class without a signature shows an Add a signature link on its cover.
A tall signature, like a fraction or a binomial, shrinks to fit the cover instead of being cut off.
Each class gets a signature, a line of math, code or text that shows big behind the class name and inks in as you study, with a progress line under it.
Halley leaves a note from your teacher on each class's cover.
Settings has a new Teaching section with six areas. Each one has its switches, your own rules, and the full instructions if you want to rewrite them.
You can give a class its own rules in Edit class.
Appearance works now. Pick a background or your own color, any font on your computer, text size, heading weight and one color for bold and italic, with a live preview.
The dark and light mode switch is gone. A light background makes the whole app light.
godspeed warns you when a linked folder is missing or has more than 500 files, and linking it again keeps the facts you already have.
Files from a linked folder show a folder mark, with Show in Finder to open them.
Sounds for the startup screen, onboarding and right or wrong answers, with one Sounds switch in Settings.
Adding class files is much faster and uses far fewer tokens. Each part of a file takes your agent one step instead of five or six, and topics are sorted once after a batch of files.
godspeed searches your class files on your computer, with no API key. Your agent finds the right pages or lecture minutes and reads just those instead of whole PDFs.
While your agent works on a reply, the lesson shows its plan, its steps and the pages it reads.
The logo forms each time you open the app, with your agent and next deadline under it.
Halley peeks from the bottom corner and rises when you hover.
Report a bug, in Settings and the Help menu, opens a GitHub issue with your app version and OS filled in.
Agent setup reminds you to turn off permission prompts so your agent can work on its own.
PDF text keeps its line breaks.
Home is the new start page. It lists every class's deadlines in one place, with a live countdown that turns red during the last day.
Exams are now deadlines. Each one has a kind (exam, homework, quiz or project), a date, an optional time and a box to mark it done. Your agent can add them from the syllabus.
Due soon in the sidebar shows the next deadlines from every class.
The class Overview shows how ready you are for each upcoming deadline.
Your agent always knows today's date and what's due.
Halley, a small comet, shows what your agent is changing in the app. Turn on Follow to go where it goes. You can rename it in Settings.
The download files have plain names, like godspeed-mac-apple-silicon.dmg, and the release page starts with a table that shows which one to download.
Reading class files and building the knowledge graph no longer gets stuck while an outside agent is teaching a lesson.
The Background agents panel tells you when no outside agent is running, and how to start one.
After an update, a What's new window lists the changes. Settings → General → Release notes shows it again.
godspeed is the new name. Claude Code, Codex or any MCP app can now be your teacher, on the plan you already pay for.
Classes: each class has its own lessons, files, knowledge graph and exams.
A new lesson layout: a step bar on top, a reading column, and an always-open Your turn panel.
The class Overview and the topic Graph show what you've covered and what to work on before each exam.
The Files page: drag files in, link a folder, and see which files you've studied.
Updates download on their own, and the Mac app is signed and notarized by Apple.
